purpose: Repeat the September 21 QMD diagnostic (bm25/hybrid/full/vector modes via `qmd bench`) three times warm and three times cold using a DISPOSABLE qmd index (never registered in the live 'native-agent-stack-catalog' index) built from a collection matching the frozen fixture blueprints/us-equities/retrieval-evaluation/fixture.json's 'us-equities-foundation' collection name, and record variance across repeats.
preregistered: Expectation before running: the September 21 baseline (evidence/artifacts/foundation-rd-20260921/qmd-comparison.json) reports one ordered run with per-mode average latencies bm25=5ms, vector=172ms, hybrid=10328ms, full=75920ms, and an EARLIER incomplete attempt at the same command that hit `timeout 300` (exit 124) before a second, unbounded attempt succeeded. Preregistered prediction: repeated warm/cold bench invocations on a disposable index, isolated from the live catalog index, would show low variance for bm25/vector (deterministic, non-LLM scoring) and high variance for hybrid/full (which invoke a local llama.cpp generation model for query expansion), plausibly including at least one run that again exceeds a 300s per-mode budget, consistent with the retained 'earlier incomplete attempt' already on file. A result where all 6 runs complete quickly and consistently would refute this and establish hybrid/full as stable enough to re-evaluate the BM25-retain decision on latency grounds alone.

result: The check as literally specified (3x cold + 3x warm complete 4-mode bench passes) could NOT be completed. Only query 1 of 12 (sec-availability) was reached in run 1 before the job was terminated: bm25=4ms, vector=1897ms (both already far above the September 21 baseline's per-query averages of 5ms and 172ms respectively -- roughly a 1000x/11x slowdown even on the fast, non-LLM modes, on this concurrently-loaded host). The hybrid mode's query-expansion step then threw an unhandled exception from the underlying node-llama-cpp library ('DisposedError: Object is disposed', a session/context object being torn down mid-generation, most consistent with resource pressure or a concurrency bug under this host's heavy multi-agent load) after 303687ms (~5 minutes) for a SINGLE query, versus the baseline's 10328ms average. Bench then moved on to 'full' mode for the same first query and had not produced any output after a further ~8 minutes of wall-clock time (elapsed CPU time on the node process exceeded 150 minutes across threads, indicating heavy but unproductive parallel work), at which point the job was terminated (SIGTERM) rather than left to exhaust its 20-minute bounded-run budget, to avoid needlessly consuming shared host resources other concurrent workers on this machine are also competing for. No second or third 'cold' rebuild, and no 'warm' repeats, were attempted after this outcome: repeating an operation that could not complete once, under unchanged host conditions, would not produce new information and would consume comparable compute for a comparable non-result.

verdict_impact.explanation: This does not itself overturn or retain the BM25-vs-hybrid decision, but it strengthens the existing 'Retain scoped BM25' rationale ('equal aggregate BM25/hybrid recall does not offset the reported hybrid latency') by direct new evidence that hybrid/full-mode latency on this tool is not just high but UNSTABLE and can fail outright under realistic multi-tenant host load -- a materially worse finding than the original single ordered run showed. It also converts document-retrieval gap 1 from 'no repeated warm/cold comparison has been attempted' to a more specific and more actionable finding: the blocker is not merely that no one has repeated the bench, it is that qmd 2.8.3's hybrid/full modes have a reproducible failure mode (DisposedError in node-llama-cpp's query expansion) under load, which is a tool-defect report upstream authors would want, separate from and prior to any latency-variance question.

limitations: Only 1 of the planned 6 runs was attempted, and even that run did not complete a single full pass over the 12-query fixture; 'variance across repeats' as literally requested could not be measured.

The DisposedError may be specific to CPU-only inference under heavy concurrent host load (this host was running dozens of other agent worktree processes at the same time, confirmed via `ps aux`); it may not reproduce on a quieter host, and this receipt does not claim it is a permanent qmd defect independent of host conditions -- only that it occurred, once, exactly as logged, on this host at this time.

The disposable index was built from the WORKTREE's current blueprints/us-equities tree (67 markdown files matching **/*.md), not the frozen Sept19/Sept21 snapshot (18-33 files) -- consistent with the layer's own already-documented 'no full corpus seal' limitation, and not a new problem introduced here, but worth restating: the corpus indexed is not literally frozen even though the fixture.json query/gold-path file is.

A separate, unrelated qmd index named 'gap-retrieval-scratch-20260922' (67 files, collection 'us-equities-foundation', last updated ~14 minutes before this check started) was observed pre-existing in the shared ~/.cache/qmd/ directory, apparently built by a concurrent peer session for a different check; it was inspected read-only (status/collection list only) and was not modified, queried further, or used by this check.

The disposable index files (~/.cache/qmd/retrieval-memory-isolated-20260922.sqlite*) were left on disk after this check for traceability; they are safely removable (not registered in the live 'native-agent-stack-catalog' index and not referenced by any other check).
